current_activity: First Allied unit to reach the Rhine: an advance detachment of combat command 3 reaches the river at Rosenau
notes: Event date: 19 November 1944 (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 419; Wikipedia). current_activity: A French incursion to Ulm on the Danube: the leading French elements reach the city ahead of the Americans
notes: Event date: 23 April 1945 (CMH The Last Offensive, p. 431: at dusk; de Lattre's notes, pp. 485-486: 19.15). Event definition: On de Lattre's order to be in Ulm by 25 April, the division's leading elements reach the first houses of Ulm on the evening of 23 April, ten hours ahead of the 44th US Division; the tricolour flies over Ulm on 24 April. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH) and de Lattre's History of the French First Army). CMH The Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 431: "The leading French platoon drew up outside Ulm at dusk on 23 April"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 482: "advancing at the double so as to be in Ulm by the 25th April"; p. 485-486: "ten hours ahead of the American units of the 44th U.S.I.D.". Location: Ulm, Baden-Württemberg with a precision of 5 km. Location support: The CMH history dates the arrival of the leading French platoon outside Ulm to dusk on 23 April without naming its division; de Lattre's notes attribute the Ulm thrust to the 1st D.B.
